draft.briefing: Hey, you're at East Fort! This street has been a busy trading centre ever since Thiruvananthapuram was the capital of the kingdom of Travancore. The old European-style fort gate opens straight onto the Padmanabhaswamy Temple.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat right here, but it's a busy commercial street, so just ask a shopkeeper where they eat.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Pazhavangadi Ganapathy Temple is 2 min away, the Methan mani clock tower 3 min, and the Padmanabhaswamy Temple about 7 min on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Come back in the evening when the East Fort Gate is lit up. It's one of the big sights of the city.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Kuthiramalika Palace, designed by the musician king Swathi Thirunal, is famous for its horse-shaped windows.

spots.name: Padmanabhaswamy Temple
spots.detail: 7 min walk · One of the 108 Divya Desams, sacred to Vishnu

spots.name: Kuthiramalika Palace
spots.detail: Close to the temple · Royal thrones, paintings and horse-shaped windows

spots.name: Pazhavangadi Ganapathy Temple
spots.detail: 2 min walk · Sculptures of 32 forms of Ganesha

legends.title: Vishnu asleep on a serpent
legends.body: The god here is Anantha Padmanabhaswamy, Vishnu in yogic sleep on his serpent Shesha. He's the family deity of the Travancore royals, and the titular Maharaja is still the temple's trustee.

legends.title: The god's old home
legends.body: The old Sreekanteswaram Temple at Puthenchantha is said to be the original home of the Lord of the newer temple near North Fort. The king and his retinue once passed it on the way to the temple's Pallivetta.

tips.title: Come back after dark.
tips.body: The lit-up East Fort Gate in the evening is a major attraction.

tips.title: Skip museums on Mondays.
tips.body: Most ticketed museums in the city are closed on Mondays, so check before you go.

story.title: An ancient temple
story.body: Historian Elamkulam Kunjan Pillai says the Pazhaya Sreekanteswaram Temple has stood since at least 1000 AD. It's an old Shiva and Vishnu temple just up the road.

story.title: A musician king
story.body: Maharaja Swathi Thirunal set up SMV School, one of the oldest in Kerala, for English education. He also designed Kuthiramalika Palace, where his music festival is still held.

story.title: A different kind of temple
story.body: The Venkatachalapathy Temple went up a minute's walk from the Padmanabhaswamy Temple's south gate. Unlike most Kerala temples, its poojas don't follow the Namboodiri tradition.

story.title: A 19-gun kingdom
story.body: Travancore became part of the Madras States Agency, ruled by a Maharaja with a hereditary 19-gun salute.

story.title: Heart of the city
story.body: Most of the old fort walls are gone, except the eastern side, which gave East Fort its name. Now it's the city's main bus stand, theatres and a whole lot of shopping.
